Adaptive Sport & Fitness Club (Winter Adaptive Games)
Since its beginnings, WAG has benefited both Queen's students and these young members of the Kingston community. In keeping with the goal of a more accepting society, Queen's is proud to say that WAG is an inclusive event for children and youth who might otherwise miss out on opportunities for physical activity. WAG emphasizes the importance of social interaction and physical activity in an environment that promotes success and emphasizes the ability to participate. Each year, the host Queen's students are increasingly encouraged by the shining abilities demonstrated by WAG participants. In fact, many student volunteers are out-run and out-played by their participant buddies in a wide range of activities. Though WAG occurs just once a year, we hope that its impact is felt throughout the year. For some children, the WAG experience provides the motivation and confidence to pursue physical activity elsewhere throughout the year.

Co-Presidents: Rachel Baker & Leeza Gibbons
Club Email: qadaptivesport@queensu.ca

Archery Club
The Archery Club aims to bring together and provide a space for those interested in archery, both experienced archers and beginners. Those who are inexperienced in archery techniques are provided with instruction and training, as well as any equipment necessary for the sport. Participants with their own equipment are encouraged to use it.

Brazilian Jiu Jitsu 
The Queen's Recreational Brazilian Jiu Jitsu seeks to introduce people to this style of martial art. Queen's Brazilian Jiu Jitsu is a martial art focused on grappling and ground work. It can be done in either the traditional martial arts uniform (gi) or in regular gym clothes. People will be introduced to a means of discipline, self-fulfillment, determination, and self-overcoming through this martial art. The goal of this club is to increase participants overall fitness while helping each person develop their own individual set of skills.

President: Julia Okerlund
Club Email: qbrazilianjj@queensu.ca

Climbing Club
The Climbing Club is a great way to get involved in the sport with regular clinics for all levels - beginner to advanced. Members of this club learn how to climb different kinds of terrain (indoor and outdoor on actual rock and ice). Outdoor trips are run on weekends with equipment provided for members. Members can also borrow harnesses for free for use at local climbing gyms.

Dance Club
The Dance Club is the largest recreational club on Queen's campus. This expansive clubs offers 30 classes a week in ballet, jazz, tap, modern, lyrical, hip hop and Queen's own "cardiofunk". Lessons are offered at many levels ranging from beginner to advanced. The year culminates with a large dance recital in March.

Equestrian Club
The Equestrian Club offers English hunter-seat equitation lessons for all levels of riders - from those who have never been around horses through to advanced riders. The club provides a casual learning environment with an emphasis on promoting a positive experience. Each session includes eight economical lessons offered once a week for an hour. Members are also invited to ride competitively through the equestrian team.

Karate Club
The Queen's Karate Club (QKC) is a recreational martial arts club that practices and instructs Okinawan Goju Ryu Karate. We welcome anyone regardless of previous experience - whether in Goju Ryu, another style, or none at all! 

The QKC strives to foster a deeper understanding of martial arts technique and philosophy, teach practical self-defence skills and provide opportunities for our members to build leadership skills. Our club offers a safe and respectful environment where everyone can progress at their own pace. Although it is not required, members will have the opportunity to progress through belt levels in Goju Ryu, which are as follows: white, yellow, orange, green, blue, brown, shodan-ho (junior black) and shodan (first degree black belt). Members can potentially earn their black belt within four years, no matter what your goal is! Classes are for anyone who is looking for a great place to exercise, work on their skills, or learn new ones. The QKC is open to anyone who wishes to participate without prejudice to nationality, race, religion, gender, or disability. Members have also had the opportunity to participate in local martial art seminars run by master instructors from across Canada

Outdoors Club
The Outdoors Club is one of the largest and most diverse clubs on campus. Membership gives access to our rental gear - we have (almost) everything you'll need for a trip! Our overnight and day-trip activities include fall and winter camping, canoeing, hiking,cross-country, downhill skiing, snow shoeing, cycling, skating, tobogganing - the list is endless! We also run whitewater kayak pool sessions. Open to all skill levels. Please email us with any questions!

Tae Kwon Do Club
The Tae Kwon Do Club provides students the opportunity to learn and practice traditional martial arts on campus. Everyone is welcome, with or without previous training and all levels of fitness. Sessions are held in a formal and non-competitive environment where each member can train at their desired level of exertion. All classes are taught by certified Black Belt Instructors.

The Tae Kwon Do Club practices the American Kang Duk Won style, a comprehensive and balanced North American martials arts system. Students learn stances, blocking, hand techniques, numerous kicks, patterns, sparring, practical self defence and awareness. Classes also include meditation, stretching, and history and philosophy while building community and being active.

Kendo Club
The Queen's University Kendo Club is a recreational club dedicated to creating a safe, welcoming, and inclusive environment where students can learn and practice the Japanese martial art of kendo. The club aims to introduce participants to the fundamentals of kendo and aspects of Japanese culture while promoting physical fitness, discipline, and personal growth. Our vision is to build a supportive kendo community at Queen's University where members can train together, develop their skills, and form meaningful friendships. The club is open to everyone regardless of prior experience, offering an accessible opportunity for all students to explore kendo in a fun and collaborative setting.
